output:
**To whoever is putting their rubbish in the bin at No. 14**

I’m putting this through every door because I don’t know who’s doing it, and I’m not going to start pointing fingers at neighbours without knowing.

For the last month or so, someone has been putting full black bags of their rubbish into my grey Greenmount Bins bin. Not the odd wrapper or a few bits — full bags, week after week.

Last Tuesday, I got home from work after a gig at about 3am to find three black bags that weren’t mine stuffed into it, including one with nappies. The lid wouldn’t even close.

My bin is charged by weight, at €0.41 a kilo. My last bill was €63.20 for two months. It’s normally around €25. I’m absolutely fuming that I’m being left to pay for someone else’s rubbish on top of my own.

The bin has **14 painted in white on the lid**, so there shouldn’t be any confusion about whose it is. It goes out on Tuesday night for Wednesday morning collection. Putting it out to be emptied is not an invitation for someone else to fill it.

I work nights. Just because I’m not home when you’re doing it doesn’t mean I won’t notice, and it doesn’t mean I’ll put up with it. I work hard for my money, and I’ve no intention of spending it getting rid of your nappies and black bags.

If you’re genuinely stuck, ask. I’ll happily tell you who to ring to sort out a bin collection. But quietly making your rubbish my expense is taking the piss.

**Whoever is doing this: stop. Simple as that.** If it carries on, I’ll be putting a padlock on the bin. I shouldn’t have to lock up my rubbish to stop someone else running up my bill.

To everyone who has nothing to do with this, apologies for the letter. I’d much rather not have had to write it.

**No. 14, Aughrim Terrace**
